title: Default-path stdin read is unwrapped, so an unreadable stdin reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_INCOMPATIBLE where --request - reports BINDING_ABSENT
description:
Filed by the LCLI-679 round-1 review and ruled out of that task scope (leader ruling, 2026-10-06: NARROW the docs to the empty-or-absent case; make NO behaviour change to agent.ts:230 in LCLI-679). UNSTARTED: do not begin until the opum-doc ruling comes back on whether these unversioned stderr markers fall under ADR-0005 section 7.1 at all.

MEASUREMENT (installed/repo build at LCLI-679 head cd8d11cb). Default path, fd 0 unreadable:
  $ bun src/cli.ts agent context pair --contract opum-agent-workflow/v1 --json 0>&1
  stderr OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_INCOMPATIBLE, exit 1
The --request - path for the same condition:
  $ bun src/cli.ts agent context pair --contract opum-agent-workflow/v1 --request - --json 0>&1
  stderr OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_BINDING_ABSENT, exit 1
So the SAME caller-visible condition is classified two ways depending on which flag path is taken, and the documented marker set tells a caller to read INCOMPATIBLE as a contract-version problem rather than as an unreadable binding.

CAUSE: src/commands/agent.ts:230 calls readFileSync(0, "utf8") UNWRAPPED when neither --request nor --request-file is set. The EBADF it throws is caught by runWorkflowBinding catch block and falls through emitBindingFailure generic branch (agent.ts:329) to INCOMPATIBLE. Only resolveBindingFile (agent.ts:311) wraps the read and attributes BINDING_ABSENT.

TWO REMEDIES, either is defensible and the choice is a contract call:
  (a) wrap the default-path read at agent.ts:230 the way resolveBindingFile does, so an unreadable stdin yields BINDING_ABSENT on both paths. This adds behaviour and changes which marker a caller sees, which is why the leader kept it out of LCLI-679.
  (b) document the split deliberately: keep INCOMPATIBLE for the default path and say so in the marker vocabulary, so callers can distinguish them on purpose rather than by accident.

DEPENDENCY: the opum-doc answer on the section 7.1 question above, since both remedies change or freeze a marker meaning.
implementationNotes: REMEDY RULED, no second round needed (DEC-165 (3), opum-doc origin/dev 14b1da7, opum-ai/opum-doc#751): an UNREADABLE stdin reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_BINDING_ABSENT on BOTH the default path and --request -, because from the adapter side no binding was supplied. Today the default path reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_INCOMPATIBLE with exit 1. So the remedy is (a): wrap the default-path read at src/commands/agent.ts:230 the way resolveBindingFile (:311) does, NOT (b) documenting the split. The dependency on the opum-doc section 7.1 question is REMOVED: DEC-165 (4) answered it — the OPUM_WORKFLOW_* markers are governed by opum-doc control-plane spec stable-redacted-errors list, not by lore-cli ADR-0005 error_type rule. This task starts next, after LCLI-679 lands, ahead of LCLI-681, 682 and 683.
